review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the related Presentable/Basic.lean and the uses of `isCardinalFiltered_aleph0_iff` and `ObjectProperty.isFinitelyPresentable_eq_isCardinalPresentable` in Presentable/Dense.lean, Directed.lean and IsCardinalFiltered.lean. The file declares no @[simp] lemmas, so it has no competing rules, rewrite cycles or unwanted expansion. The only candidate was the rfl lemma `ObjectProperty.isFinitelyPresentable_eq_isCardinalPresentable`. Dense.lean uses it only through explicit `rw`, followed by `infer_instance`. No use shows a simp call stuck on `isFinitelyPresentable`. The `<;> simp only [isCardinalFiltered_aleph0_iff] at *` calls are local, targeted rewrites that are not part of any global simp set. Marking the rfl lemma @[simp] would turn a deliberately opaque def into its cardinal form everywhere. That could be unwanted, and I found no evidence of a benefit. I found no justified finding. I could not run Lean, so I cannot rule out that a missing simp lemma matters in other files that I did not search.
